description.narrative: Limited access to reliable and affordable electricity is one of the most binding constraints to economic growth and shared prosperity in Burkina Faso. With a Gross National Income (GNI) per capita of barely US$ 800, Burkina Faso is among the 20 poorest countries in the world.. Poverty is overwhelmingly concentrated in rural areas, which are home to 90 percent of poor households, and is largely attributed to underemployment, limited social inclusion, low agricultural productivity and poor access to electricity. Burkina Faso need to address two interlinked challenges in the energy sector: a very low access levels and a very high cost of electricity supply. Average electricity tariff of US$ 0.24 per kWh, one of the highest in in the sub-region, is below the overall cost of electricity service estimated at US$ 0.26 per kWh, for which fuel costs account for more than 40 percent. The gap is bridged through recurrent implicit fuel subsidies, that amounted an average yearly US$55m over the past three years, weighing heavily on limited fiscal resources. This, in turn, limits public resources available for investments on the access agenda and to fight energy poverty, in particular in rural areas. As a result, the access rate has stagnated over the past decade and remained consistently below regional standards, notably in rural areas, which are exposed to acute poverty and face heightened security challenges. The theory of change is that Burkina would seek to gradually reduce operating subsidies for the people currently connected to the grid, which are essentially located in urban areas and are relatively well-off, and shift public funds towards increasing access.Given the magnitude of the financing needs, the proposed project will focus on developing a rapid and scalable electricity access expansion approach, harnessing solar energy potential to reduce electricity costs and mobilizing private capital at scale. The focus of this proposed Project is to advance on the three interrelated pillars and develop business models that can be replicated at scale. In its efforts to increase access, the Project design will be informed by the recommendations of the recently-completed audit of COOPELS, which sought to improve the bankability of investments of mini-grids, and on an updated geospatial mapping to implement grid densification for productive uses. In addition, the diversification of the energy mix towards cheaper domestic solar potential is critical to gradually reduce recurrent subsidies and bridge the sector operating cost-revenue gap. The Project will support the development of a well-structured solar tender, which is expected to demonstrate the value for money of a competitive process, and result in lower generation costs.This project seeks approval to provide additional financing (AF) of US$187 million equivalent and a grant from the Energy Sector Management Assistance Program (ESMAP) multi-donor trust fund (MDTF) in the amount of US$2.5 million to the Solar Energy and Access Project (Deploiement ?du Solaire ?a ?Large Echelle et ?d’’Electrification ?Rurale, ?SOLEER; ?P166785). ?SOLEER was approved by the World Bank Board on June 22, 2021. ?The project is financed by ?the credit ?IDA-6919 for EUR69.1 million (approximately US$72.8 million ?equivalent), US$89 million loan from the Clean Technology Fund (CTF, TF-0B5740), US$3 million grant from the Clean Technology Fund (TF-0B5738) and US$0.7 million grant from the Global Infrastructure Fund (GIF, TF0B5744). The project became effective on June 22, 2022. ?The project development ?objective ?(PDO) ?is to increase access to electricity services in selected rural areas and the availability of solar energy in Burkina Faso by leveraging private finance. ?IDA resources have a 65 percent disbursement rate as of ?June 30, 2026. CTF and GIF resources combined have a 24 percent disbursement rate and is 90 percent committed. Contracts worth US$ 46 million equivalent are at final stages of procurement. The proposed AF will increase electricity access impact, expand the project's scope and mitigate cost overruns. ?The proposed AF will provide US$187 million from the International Development Association (IDA) and US$2.5 million from the ESMAP Clean Cooking Fund to: (ai) provide electricity access ?through grid and off-grid solutions to an additional ?1 million people, including electrifying social infrastructure (scale-up); (bii) finance productive use solutions to cooperatives, medium and small scale businesses (scale-up); (ciii) finance cost overruns for installing equipment to facilitate the evacuation of the 150MW solar power plants (cost overrun); and (div) introduce a new sub-component to provide clean cooking solutions to around 100,000 households (design change).
To increase access to electricity services and the availability of solar energy in Burkina Faso by leveraging private finance.?

condition.narrative: FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(a)/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(a)/GA GIF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(a)/GA CTF Annex ArticleII, 2.03, A.2(a): the Recipient shall establish, and maintain throughout the course of the Project implementation, a PMU within theMinistry in charge of energy with mandate, composition and resources acceptable to the Association.

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(d)/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(d)/GA GIF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(d)/GA CTF Annex ArticleII, 2.03, A.2(d):: Not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, the internal auditor, referred to in sub-paragraph (c)of this paragraph shall have been recruited and appointed.

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(e)/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(e)/GA GIF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(e)/GA CTF Annex ArticleII, 2.03, A.2(e): Not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, the external auditor shall have recruited and appointedon the basis of terms of reference, qualifications, integrity and experience acceptable to the Association.

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(f)/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(f)/GA GIF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 2(f)/GA CTF Annex ArticleII, 2.03, A.2(f): Not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall have acquired, installed andcustomized a computerized accounting software, satisfactory to the Association.

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.A, 3(a)/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 3(a)/GA GIF Schedule 2, Section I.A, 3(a)/GA CTF Annex ArticleII, 2.03, A.3(a): No later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall establish and maintain, at all timesduring the implementation of the Project, a Project steering committee with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory tothe Association.

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.C, 1/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.C, 1/GA CTF Annex Article II, 2.03, C.1: To facilitate the carryingout of Part 1 of the Project, the Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date enter into animplementation agreement with ABER satisfactory to the Association, vesting responsibility in ABER for the technical management ofPart 1 of the Project, and specifying ABER roles and responsibilities ("ABER Project Implementation Agreement").

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.C, 2/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.C, 2/GA CTF Annex Article II, 2.03, C.2: To facilitate the carryingout of Part 2 of the Project, the Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, enter into animplementation agreement with SONABEL satisfactory to the Association, vesting responsibility in SONABEL for the technicalmanagement of Part 2 of the Project, and specifying SONABEL roles and responsibilities ("SONABEL Project ImplementationAgreement").

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.C, 3/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.C, 3/GA CTF Annex Article II, 2.03, C.3: To facilitate the carryingout of Part 2 of the Project, the Recipient shall ensure that, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, SONABEL hasrecruited and appointed a social development specialist on the basis of terms of reference, qualifications, integrity, andexperience acceptable to the Association.

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.D, 2/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.D, 2/GA GIF Schedule 2, Section I.C, 2/GA CTF Annex Article II,2.03, D: the Recipient shall, and shall cause ABER and SONABEL to, ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with theEnvironmental and Social Commitment Plan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Association. To this end, the Recipient shall, andshall cause ABER and SONABEL to, ensure that: (a) the measures and actions specified in the ESCP are implemented with due diligenceand efficiency, as provided in the ESCP; (b) sufficient funds are available to cover the costs of implementing the ESCP; (c)policies and procedures are maintained, and qualified and experienced staff in adequate numbers are retained to implement the ESCP,as provided in the ESCP; and (d) the ESCP, or any provision thereof, is not amended, repealed, suspended or waived, except as theAssociation shall otherwise agree in writing, as specified in the ESCP, and ensure that the revised ESCP is disclosed promptlythereafter.

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.D, 6/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.D, 6/GA GIF Schedule 2, Section I.C, 6/GA CTF Annex Article II,2.03, D.5: the Recipient shall establish, publicize, maintain and operate an accessible grievance mechanism, to receive andfacilitate resolution of concerns and grievances of Project-affected people, and take all measures necessary and appropriate toresolve, or facilitate the resolution of, such concerns and grievances, in a manner acceptable to the Association.

FA IDA Schedule 2, Section I.D, 8/FA CTF Schedule 2, Section I.D, 8/GA GIF Schedule 2, Section I.C, 8/GA CTF Annex Article II,2.03, D.8: The Recipient shall, and shall cause ABER and SONABEL to refrain for carrying out any works under the Project until andunless the relevant RAP, as approved by the Association, has been duly disclosed in country and in the Association's website.

title.narrative: Percentage of women working in mini-grid operations

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the percentage of women working in mini-grid operations in localities supported by the project (share in the total workforce). Overall female employment in the energy sector is very low in Burkina Faso. This holds for newly established opertions and even though private sector participants have cited pilot operations where women have been employed for these roles successfully. However, similar initiatives appear only to be occurring as pilots and therefore the baseline was determined to be 0

title.narrative: Share of female-headed households provided with new or improved electricity services

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the the percentage of female-headed households in the rural areas of Burkina Faso with access to new or improved electricity services as a result of the project. Given the gap identified in energy access equity would be achieved if FHHs are connected at the same rate as MHHs. Therefore, under the project a target has been set of reaching 7 percent which is the prevalence of FHHs in the rural areas of Burkina Faso. The baseline is listed as zero as the gap has been identified above but the baseline for the chosen location is unknown. Focus will be placed on cross-validating the post-electrification findings through possible surveys and focus-group discussions to track project.
